# Lab notes: regenerating fungal-derived adsorption membranes after PFAS capture

## Week 12
Fungal-derived membranes captured more than 90 % of PFOA from spiked tap water at 1 µg L-1 in batch tests.

Regeneration with methanol recovered only 60 % of the capacity after three cycles; the solvent waste is a problem for scale-up.

## Week 13
Idea: degrade the captured PFAS directly on the membrane instead of washing it out. Needs a photocatalyst that works under visible light and does not damage the fungal matrix.

<!-- page -->

## Week 14
No photocatalysis expertise in the group. Possible collaborators should have experience with visible-LED photocatalysts for persistent organic pollutants.

## Next steps
- Test thermal stability of the membrane up to 80 °C.
- Look for partners in photocatalytic water treatment.
